incidents.vector: International law enforcement (Operation Endgame) seized 106 servers and domains behind the SocGholish framework, which injected fake browser-update JavaScript into hacked websites to broker access for ransomware crews.
incidents.impact: Authorities disrupted a near-decade-old initial-access operation used by ransomware groups including Russia's Evil Corp, and remediated 14,971 compromised sites, mostly WordPress.

incidents.vector: Two UK members of the Scattered Spider group infiltrated TfL's network in September 2024 using stolen credentials and social engineering; both pleaded guilty on the first day of trial.
incidents.impact: The 2024 breach forced all 28,000 TfL staff to reset passwords in person, exposed Oyster customer refund data, and cost roughly £29M ($38M); one defendant also admitted hacking U.S. healthcare provider SSM Health.

incidents.victim: Major U.S. banks and their customers
incidents.vector: An Algerian national known as 'SPOX' ran two black-market sites (market0day.com, spoxy.us) selling stolen financial credentials and custom phishing kits targeting U.S. banks; he was extradited from Spain and charged.
incidents.impact: Prosecutors say the operation defrauded thousands of victims and funneled roughly $900,000 through a cryptocurrency account over three years.

incidents.vector: Microsoft DART found a single intrusion involving two unrelated actors; one group (tracked as Storm-2603) exploited on-prem SharePoint flaws since mid-2025, then used Velociraptor, Cloudflare tunneling, Zoho Assist and SSH-over-VS Code for persistence.
incidents.impact: Parallel ransomware and stealthy persistence activity blended in one network, complicating attribution and response; case detailed in Microsoft's ninth cyberattack-series report.

incidents.victim: Government, critical infrastructure and multinationals (194 countries)
incidents.vector: The 'FortiBleed' dataset exposed valid admin and SSL-VPN credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate firewalls; actors ran ~1.16 billion credential attempts, intercepted VPN auth hashes, and cracked them on a 45-GPU cluster to reach internal Active Directory.
incidents.impact: Confirmed compromises span government, telecom, finance, healthcare and manufacturing, including a Turkish NATO defense contractor; many devices remained online with exposed management interfaces. ACSC issued a critical alert urging immediate credential rotation.

incidents.vector: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects tied to the Silver Fox cybercrime group, which spread its trojan (ValleyRAT/Winos) via malspam and fake app-download sites to deploy infostealers and remote-access trojans.
incidents.impact: Arrests across five provinces dismantled much of China's largest domestic cybercrime crew, including the malware author and phishing-site operators who stole victims' online funds and assets.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research community
incidents.vector: A PRC-nexus actor (tracked as UNC6508) abused Google Workspace compliance rules and vulnerabilities in the REDCap research platform to collect intelligence, remaining undetected for over a year.
incidents.impact: The campaign targeted institutions conducting AI, cyber, medical and national-defense research to harvest sensitive research data.

incidents.vector: Attackers 'adopted' more than 1,900 abandoned (orphaned) packages on the unofficial Arch User Repository and modified install scripts to pull a malicious npm/Bun payload delivering a rootkit and credential harvester.
incidents.impact: The infostealer collects browser, Electron-app and developer secrets/access keys; the campaign was still expanding and actively evading detection at time of reporting, with infection counts unknown.

incidents.vector: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko, extradited from Ireland, pleaded guilty to a wire-fraud conspiracy tied to deploying Conti ransomware that infected over 1,000 computers and networks.
incidents.impact: Conti attacked more than 1,000 victims and netted at least $150 million in ransom payments; the guilty plea marks a milestone in international ransomware prosecution.

incidents.vector: The ShinyHunters group (tracked as UNC6240) exploited CVE-2026-35273, a critical Oracle PeopleSoft RCE, as a zero-day against Environment Management Hub endpoints, deploying custom MeshCentral agents and a defacement/lateral-movement script.
incidents.impact: Mandiant notified 100+ exposed organizations, mostly U.S. higher-education institutions; stolen data was published on ShinyHunters' leak site. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on June 12.

incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese intelligence used 13 fake 'consulting company' websites with AI-generated content, professional networking sites and online payment platforms to lure current and former clearance holders into sharing sensitive information.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized all 13 domains, disrupting a scheme designed to recruit or coerce Americans with access to classified and sensitive U.S. government information.

incidents.vector: Meta says it disrupted a new NSO Group spear-phishing campaign that tried to lure WhatsApp users into clicking malicious links leading to an external exploit site, in violation of a U.S. court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta filed for contempt against NSO and urged lawmakers to keep the sanctioned firm on the U.S. Entity List, citing renewed targeting of secure-messaging users.
